concept: A mesh is a piece of the world, not a control: colour pooled in four places and melted together, used as a scene, as media or as the light a coloured object casts. The system still owns no hue; a product brings its own colours to it.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a two-stop linear brand gradient used as a fake mesh on a button or a hero (the 2020s SaaS gradient)
default_to_avoid.why_not: a linear sweep has one direction and no depth, and on a control it gives the system a hue of its own, which P1 rules out
default_to_avoid.kind: mesh gradient, freeform gradient, aurora background

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: the mesh is a scene or media, so its hue is the world's; a product sets its own colours through four variables and Pane ships presets, never a fill for a control

derivation.consequence: legibility comes from dimming and blurring the backdrop (brightness, blur) inside a smoked body thick enough that a pane reads as a slab of glass, with the scene softened behind it
derivation.form: the pools are blurred on their own layer until no edge is left, so glass over a mesh softens a field of colour and has nothing sharp to fight

derivation.consequence: corners are continuous and nest, so an inner surface's radius is the outer radius minus the padding between them and a pane inside a pane reads as inside it; controls are full pills because they are held in the hand
derivation.form: a mesh takes the corner of whatever it fills (a cover, an icon, a stage) and its ambient light follows that corner

derivation.consequence: long ease-out curves (420 to 640ms) for arriving and hovering, a shorter one (200ms) for pressing because a press is a reply; under reduced motion every duration is zero at the token level
derivation.form: a mesh does not drift on its own; things settle, so it is still unless the product animates it

variants.reason: A is the reference read straight: colour placed where the light is and melted, which is what makes it a mesh (P1 depth). B keeps a ring on every pool and reads as spotlights. C swirls around one centre and cannot put a colour where the light comes from (P3 depth: one light from above).

root.why: the box the mesh fills; it holds the content placed on the mesh and takes the corner it is given

paint.why: the clipped layer that holds the blurred pools, so the blur never leaks past the corner

glow.why: the ambient light under a mesh object: the same pools, blurred and lowered, the colour of the object lighting what is under it

ember.why: a warm preset: amber and rose over a plum low point

tide.why: a cool preset: aqua and sky over an indigo low point

dusk.why: an evening preset: lilac and rose over a deep navy low point

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop the pools and keep a plain canvas, so content on a mesh stays readable
